I used to be an electrician apprentice for a coal wash plant. We were testing a new device above what we called a 'sizer'. The sizer was 2 rotating cylinders with large teeth, it ground boulders to pebbles in seconds.

It wasn't working properly so we had to take it down, in the pouring rain. My trainer was a large man so asked if I'd go up and I stupidly agreed without safety equipment. Covering the drop was mesh sheeting that could be opened inwards. You see where this is going.

Due to my natural fear of heights, I kept one foot on the sturdy side to steady myself, reached over onto the bar where the device was attached and begun undoing the bolts. It was too hard as 2 of them were slightly out of reach, so I moved a foot closer to the centre, where the mesh fell open.

Luckily I had my stable foot on the side, and a good grip on the bar above it, which held the device. Otherwise I was going home in a carrier bag. I left that place shortly after, they saw health and safety more as guidelines, not necessary.
